answer: Admission proof-of-work at the gate: each identity must submit a hash puzzle calibrated to ~40 CPU-hours on commodity hardware. A comet of fresh signups can't reuse one solution, since the bridge commits each nonce to the identity's key. Detection tightens difficulty whenever a sparrow-sized cohort joins within one epoch. Attacker cost: 10k identities ≈ 400k CPU-hours ≈ $18k in spot compute, recurring per epoch — real users pay once. Works because forging identities is priced above their marginal governance yield.
